entries.subject: DAMIT 5661: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: DAMIT model 5661, version 2019-10-23, pole (229°, 31°), period 10.2536 h, taken unchanged from the archive.

entries.subject: Physical scale
entries.finding: 107.795 ± 1.571 km, effective diameter of a sphere fitted to thermal infrared measurements. JPL lists a diameter of 107.795 ± 1.571 km, from NEOWISE (Masiero et al. 2012, ApJ 759, L8; PDS bundle neowise_diameters_albedos 2.0). The thermal sphere diameter is transferred to the mesh as its volume-equivalent diameter.

entries.subject: PDS SBN catalogue values that disagree with the factsheet or are not shown
entries.finding: Shown size Display reference radius "53.9 km (size-calibrated model)" (jpl-small-body-database) differs from the Small Bodies Occultations V4.0 record 339, DAMIT model 5661 diameter 91 ± 6 km (volume-equivalent; DAMIT model 5661 fitted to 5 occultations); the shown value is kept.

entries.subject: Gerlinde whole-disc color
entries.finding: Gaia Collaboration, Galluccio et al. (2023) published the mean of 24 Gaia epoch spectra of the unresolved disc: reflectance against the Sun in 16 bands from 374 to 1034 nm, 1 at 550 nm (0.935 at 462 nm, 1.011 at 638 nm). The shape is painted in that one color (#32312f in sRGB) through the shared disc-integrated-color method, scaled to the 3.1% geometric albedo JPL lists (± 0.4%), from NEOWISE (Masiero et al. 2012, ApJ 759, L8; PDS bundle neowise_diameters_albedos 2.0). It is one mean, not a map. Tinaut-Ruano et al. (2023), A&A 669, L14, found Gaia DR3 reflectances slightly too red at wavelengths shorter than 550 nm; the bands are used as published, without that paper's correction.
